The '''Knossa Branch Library''' was a satellite facility of the [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Great Jedi Library]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]]. Located in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Knossa/Legends|Knossa]], the branch library provided immediate access to the collection of the Great Library without having to make the long journey out of the city.

==History==
[[File:OssusLibrarypotj.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Floor plan of the Great Library's Knossa Branch propagated and sold by the con artist [[Skavak/Legends|Skavak]] as a depiction of the Great Library itself]]
When the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] commissioned the construction of the [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Great Jedi Library]] circa [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] in the remote [[Ooroo Canyon/Legends|Ooroo Canyon]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]] sought to build a branch of this library within the city limits of [[Knossa/Legends|Knossa]] for easy and quick access to the collective works of the Great Library. Where the Great Library's collection was made up of ancient scrolls, treasures, and artifacts, the Knossa Branch provided remote access to the digitized collection through the use of [[Holobook/Legends|holobooks]] and computer terminals. To look at a scroll or an artifact, a scholar at the branch library had the option of remotely controlling a droid at the Great Library to look through hard copies of non-digitized works. [[Jedi librarian/Legends|Jedi librarians]] patrolled the halls of the Knossa Branch and were available by appointment to assist or conduct a conference with the Great Library for deeper research.<ref name="NoP" />

When the [[Cron Supernova/Legends|Cron Supernova]] wiped all life from the planet in [[3996 BBY]], the Knossa Branch was left in ruins. Later, the con artist [[Skavak/Legends|Skavak]] sold false floor plans, schematics, and maps on the black market. These maps often confused the Great Library with the Knossa Branch and the [[Eye of Ashlanae/Legends|Eye of Ashlanae]], making it hard for historians to get an accurate idea of the actual appearance of the facilities.<ref name="NoP" />

==Layout and architecture==
Erected in the rocky foothills of the [[Eocho Mountains/Legends|Eocho Mountains]] within the ancient Jedi city [[Knossa/Legends|Knossa]], the Knossa Branch Library was a squat building carved out of unadorned dense stone, making it appear as if the complex was a natural feature of the hill. Crowned by four thick, domed towers, the building's upper levels were perched on top of a stone ziggurat. The complex featured four main levels, as well as three sublevels, all of which contained material ranging from Pre-Republic time to the modern history of [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]]. The carved stairs leading to the main gates were unbarred, as were the doors, in line with Master Odan-Urr's belief that the knowledge prized by the Jedi should not be kept from any who sought it. With the exception of the highest level, the building blocked out all natural light; artificial light kept the building at a constantly even light so the passage of the suns' light did not increase the weariness of a devoted learner.<ref name="POTJ" />

Access to the Knossa Branch was granted through a large entryway in the southern face of the complex. The first level of the library building was dedicated to peaceful study and cool reflection; its thick, utilitarian walls held a two-story arcade of stained-glass windows detailing the events of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] while [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojectors]] displayed some of the archive's greatest treasures. Classrooms and lecture halls were on the first level, as were a collection of study chambers where [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] alike could ponder long-forgotten lore in the still silence of the dark stone building.<ref name="POTJ" /> Conference rooms allowed librarians and researchers alike to meet with staff at the Great Library in real time and seek guidance in deeper research.<ref name="NoP" /> On the second level, highly ranked [[Lore Keeper]]s oversaw the many [[Jedi Researcher|researchers]] and librarians that maintained the stacks, the massive shelving systems that held the Order's collection of [[Datacard/Legends|datacards]] and reader tapes.<ref name="GORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> A stone balustrade wrapped around the balcony that overlooked the arcade and main entrance below.<ref name="POTJ" /> The third and fourth floors of the building contained the vast Archives of the Order, delicately cataloged by tireless [[Jedi archivist/Legends|archivists]] in a system designed by Odan-Urr.<ref name="GORW" />

Sprouting from the fourth floor and accessible by spiraling stairwells were four wide towers containing artifacts sorted by era, all of which spanned what would later be considered the [[Pre-Republic era|Pre-Republic]] and [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Eras]].<ref name="GORW" /> The southeast tower, or Pre-Hyperdrive Tower, contained information gathered from civilizations which were bound to their world or [[Star system/Legends|star system]] before the invention of the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] circa [[25,053 BBY]]. Following the chronological order the northwest, or Pre-Republic Tower housed artifacts that detailed the political state of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] before the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was born in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. The northeast and southeast towers were known as the Early-Republic and Mature-Republic Towers respectively.<ref name="POTJ" />
